cards.text: Paul, an apostle of Jesus, is writing a letter to the believers in Rome (Romans 1:1, 7). He's been talking about God's law and his own life with it (Romans 7:7-13). Now he picks it back up with something he says we all know: the law is spiritual.

cards.question: Paul says the law is spiritual. Then he turns to himself. How does Paul describe himself?

answers.text: Unspiritual and sold as a slave to sin
Spiritual and ready to keep the law
Strong and free from the pull of sin

cards.text: Then Paul says something anybody with a snooze button understands: "I do not understand what I do." Your OWN thumb hits snooze on the alarm YOU set, and you're lying there like, whose thumb IS that?

cards.question: Paul says he does exactly what he wants to do and stays away from what he hates.

cards.text: Then Paul thinks it through: if he does what he doesn't want to do, what does that say about God's law?

cards.question: If Paul does what he doesn't want to do, what does he say he's admitting about God's law?

answers.text: That the law is too hard

cards.question: Paul says that in that case, it's no longer really him doing it. It's ___ living in him that does it.

cards.text: Paul gets even more honest: he knows nothing good lives in him, that is, in his flesh. This is NOT a highlight reel, friend, this is the blurry photo with his eyes half shut, and he POSTED it.

cards.question: Paul says he has no desire at all to do what is good.

cards.text: Paul circles back: he keeps doing the evil he doesn't want, and then that line again, it's sin living in him that does it. I KNOW this loop, friend: every night I tell myself NO tasting the dough, and every morning the bowl is HALF EMPTY.

cards.question: After going around and around, Paul says he's discovered a principle. What is it?

answers.text: When he wants to do good evil is right there with him
When he wants to do good it gets a little easier
When he obeys the law sin leaves him alone

cards.question: Deep down, in his inner being, Paul says he ___ in God's law.

cards.text: But Paul isn't done. He sees another law in there, and it is picking a FIGHT.

cards.question: Paul sees another law at work in his ___, warring against the law of his ___.
Paul says this other law at work in his body holds him captive to the law of sin that dwells within him.

cards.text: Paul has been honest this whole time, and now it all pours out: "What a wretched man I am!" No joke from me here, friend, because I've been stuck in the dark and I know that cry.

cards.question: Paul cries out that he's wretched, held captive by sin. What does he ask?

answers.text: Who will rescue him from this body of death
Who will lift the weight of the law from him
Who will judge him for this war within

cards.question: Right after that cry, Paul's tone turns and he gives thanks. Who does Paul thank?

answers.text: God through Jesus Christ our Lord
Moses who gave Israel the law
Gamaliel who taught him the law

cards.question: Paul sums it up by saying that with his mind he serves the law of sin, and with his flesh he serves the law of God.

findings.problem: The distractors do not fit the sentence naturally: “he doubts in God’s law” and “he grumbles in God’s law” are not believable alternatives. This leaves “delights” as the only answer that reads correctly, making it stand out.

rule.text: Wrong answers for what someone does or says only need to be believable.

findings.problem: “Body” and “mind” are aspects of Paul, while “fathers,” “people,” and “words” are not comparable alternatives for those blanks. The distractors make implausible completions and cause the correct pair to stand out instead of offering meaningful choices.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.
